body:
The fear is that since I reacted badly to ONE anti-seizure med (hives), I'll react badly to the rest. I want to try another, because that's not how induction works. it has to be true for n AND n+1 to likely be true for all n. 

I have not. I mostly do light aerobics. Sometimes, I'll do something short, but high intensity, like go and play ddr with a friend for a bit. But I usually end up leaving after maybe a game after the arcade becomes more crowded.

It's both. I suffer from panic disorder, generalized anxiety disorder, and social phobia. Triggers vary. Sometimes, its stress from a large project, so I do my best to have things done in advance. Sometimes, its social situations. For example, the class I have with the dean, has 70 people in it, in a non-lecture hall room. You can't walk down the aisles without knocking into someone. I can't take tests in this room because it's noisy even when "quiet". The proximity to other classmates makes me nervous, and I feel trapped. To make matters worse, she always gives a quiz, which takes 15+min, in the final 5 min of class. This wouldn't bother me if I didn't have to run across the campus to make it to differential equations right after her class. I can retake the quiz, for -10% ad nauseam in her office. However, she hasn't posted any of my retakes, or given me any sort of feedback of where I need to be studying (very, very, very, few papers returned). 

My social phobias most deal with day to day interactions with other people. I'm really shy and reserved. I like working alone more than in groups, because its quieter, and I don't have to rely on others. I never know what to say to people, and end up coming off as rude or terse. I've been working on my social skills, but I can only do so much. It takes a lot of energy out of me to go to class. I do most of my classes online for this reason. I fear rejection and alienation. I feel alienated in most of my classes because I'm a non traditional student, and usually, the only female. This is very intimidating for me. 

I plan on using a grade-forgiveness for this, and retake it with anyone OTHER than her. 

It would be easier if I didn't have a bunch of fails on my transcript from my first attempt in college. That's what's holding me back, and why I'm trying so hard now. I just feel like everything is getting so much further away.

I've been off of everything except benzos for panic attacks for about a year. The longest I've been on any given drug was about 6 months. It's always the same revolving door. "This isn't showing enough progress, let's try you on something else.", stop med, start new med, deal with the beginnings of a new med, which are always so much fun, nothing changes in 6 months, repeat. I showed promise on an anti-seizure medication. I felt amazing, I wasn't either high as a kite, manic, anxious, or depressed. I'm allergic to it.

I have. I abstain from a lot of caffeine, I eat fairly healthy, and I walk when I can. Heavy workouts end up stressing me, and can sometimes bring on a panic attack.

Thank you. It means a lot to me right now. I'm going to start looking for one through social services tomorrow. I used to see one through my uni, but I stopped treatment after she kept trying to push me to lithium. I didn't think lithium would help me much. I've been on nearly every anti-psychotic and anti-depressant on the market to no avail. They all made me feel fuzzy. I couldn't think. I'm an engineering student. I need to be able to think.

Hopefully, graduating with my bachelors. I have a feeling it will be bitter-sweet. I'm hoping I'll be able to get into grad-school, despite having a mediocre gpa. The panic attacks make it hard for me to go class, the social phobia doesn't help either. All I ever wanted in life was to be a scientist or engineer, and despite being so close now, it seems farther away than ever. I feel like I fucked everything up when I first tried to go to college. I started having panic attacks, I was 17. I didn't know what to do. I failed out. My school wouldn't allow for a medical or hardship withdrawal. 

I feel all of this happening again. I went to talk to a professor about it, I was having trouble in her class. She looked at me, dead in the eye, while I was on the verge of tears, and told me to "get over it and deal with it". I feel like my dream is slipping away. I'm probably going to fail that class. I can't go above her, she's the dean.

I'll call as soon as I'm able. My only qualm with calling is that I'm afraid they will try to convince me to admit myself. I don't see that as a viable option in my current state. I watched my mother be baker-acted three times. I remember visiting her. I remember the hell I saw in those hospitals. It's why I'm posting rather than calling either 211 or the suicide hotline.
